prop:bloch-group-quotient-construction:
Proposition Concrete construction of B(F) as the free abelian quotient by the pentagon subgroup (closes substantive Mathlib gap 1).

The Bloch group BlochGroup F for a field-like type F admits a concrete Lean construction as the quotient

  B(F) \;:=\; \mathrm{FreeAbelianGroup}\bigl(\mathrm{PreBlochElement}\,F\bigr)
            \;\big/\; \mathrm{pentagonSubgroup},

where PreBlochElement F carries the pre-Bloch elements (val ≠ 0 and val ≠ 1) and pentagonSubgroup is the AddSubgroup.closure of the five-term pentagon-relation generators. The quotient inherits an AddCommGroup structure from the QuotientAddGroup instance in Mathlib. It carries a canonical projection quot : PreBlochGroup F →+ BlochGroup F and satisfies the standard universal property.

See Table for the Lean structure.

This construction yields a genuine AddCommGroup rather than a typeclass ansatz. The carrier types admit a real Lean construction. The HasBlochGroup ℝ instance is concretely inhabited.

The unconstrained PentagonShape F accepts arbitrary five-tuples of pre-Bloch elements. This makes pentagonRelationGenerators too permissive. Degenerate shapes with repeated entries trivialize the quotient. A ValidPentagonShape F predicate must constrain PentagonShape F to enforce the Rogers-form constraints:

  e_3 \;\equiv\; e_2 / e_1, \quad
  e_4 \;\equiv\; (1 - e_2^{-1})/(1 - e_1^{-1}), \quad
  e_5 \;\equiv\; (1 - e_2)/(1 - e_1).

These constraints derive from a valid Rogers pair (x, y) \in F^\times \times F^\times with x \neq y, x \neq 0, x \neq 1, y \neq 0, and y \neq 1. This derivation requires decidability of the pentagon-domain conditions on F, a pentagon-shape map F \times F \to \mathrm{PentagonShape}\,F, and the restriction of pentagonRelationGenerators to the ValidPentagonShape F subtype. The structural skeleton accommodates this restriction via the validity predicate and the constrained range.

The conditional-class chain anchored by prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness brings BlochSuslinUniqueness closer to unconditional inhabitation. The remaining work includes the pentagon identity proof for \mathrm{Cl}_2 on the unit-circle subset, Bloch-Wigner regulator D \otimes \mathbb{Q} injectivity, and the Suslin map K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}.

Archimedean specialisation. The generic \mathrm{BlochGroup}[\mathrm{Field}\ F] construction instantiates the pentagon and Bloch-group relation at \mathbb{R}.

Remark Community Library 1 (HeckeTemperleyLieb): Iwahori--Hecke rewriting, Markov radicals, and Young--Hoefsmit representations. HeckeTemperleyLieb packages the algebraic and representation-theoretic formalisation of type-A_{n-1} Iwahori--Hecke algebras H_n(q) (jones1987, wenzl1988) and their Temperley--Lieb quotients TL_n(q) as a standalone Mathlib4 extension:

  • Kang--Lee--Lee--Oh Gröbner--Shirshov normal forms (NotAGSBasis, HeckeAlgebra). Proves the explicit n = 4 counterexample establishing that the naive quadratic Hecke plus braid relations fail Diamond Lemma confluence on B_4^+, and formalises the completed Kang--Lee--Lee--Oh rewriting system (kangleeleeoh2002) together with single-pass normal forms for monotone Coxeter chains (SL2ChebyshevTrace).
  • Markov trace radical and Temperley--Lieb quotient (TemperleyLiebTower, BorromeanMarkovTrace). Constructs the Jones--Ocneanu Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M at loop weight z = q^3/(q^2+1), proves exact vanishing of the three-row Wedderburn weight y_{(1^3)} = 0 and Gram determinant \det G = 0 for n \ge 3, and establishes the radical isomorphism TL_n(q) \cong H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\tau_q of Catalan dimension C_n.
  • Young--Hoefsmit seminormal matrices and Schur elements (ProtonQ3SchurElement, CrossNucleonPairWedderburnZRemoval). Formalises standard Young tableaux axial distances, seminormal generator matrices (hoefsmit1974, ram1991), central characters \chi^\lambda, and hook-content Schur weights over \mathbb{Q}(q).
rem:lean-lib-twisted-frobenius-hopf:
Remark Community Library 2 (TwistedFrobeniusHopf): Nakayama-twisted Frobenius--Hopf algebras and Woronowicz differential calculi. TwistedFrobeniusHopf formalises non-symmetric Frobenius and Hopf algebra structures where classical untwisted trace symmetry or antipode involutivity (S^2 = \mathrm{id}) fails (kock2004, woronowicz1989):

  • Nakayama-twisted Frobenius pairing (TwistedFrobeniusTower, FrobeniusHopfData). Defines ambidextrous Frobenius algebras equipped with an explicit Nakayama automorphism \nu \in \mathrm{Aut}(A) satisfying \langle a, b \rangle_F = \langle b, \nu(a) \rangle_F, instantiated concretely on Sweedler's four-dimensional Hopf algebra H_4, Taft's n^2-dimensional Hopf algebras T_n(\zeta), and O_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) where S^2 \neq \mathrm{id}.
  • Twisted \ast-Frobenius positive cones (StarFrobeniusPositiveData). Proves that the generator inversion map T_w \mapsto T_{w^{-1}}^{-1} is not R-linear at q \neq \pm 1, and constructs the sesquilinear \ast-pairing \langle X, Y \rangle_{\tau,\ast} = \tau(X^\dagger Y) descending to a positive-definite inner product on A / \mathrm{rad}\,\tau.
  • Bicovariant differential calculus dimension obstructions (CalculusDimensionObstruction). Formalises Woronowicz's left-covariant and bicovariant first-order differential calculi on quantum groups, distinguishing the three-dimensional left-covariant 3D calculus from the four-dimensional 4\mathrm{D}_\pm bicovariant calculi on \mathrm{SU}_q(2).
rem:lean-lib-toric-conic-opt:
Remark Community Library 3 (ToricConicOpt): Ordered-field conic duality, symmetry-reduced certificates, and toric Gröbner bases. ToricConicOpt provides solver-external linear, conic, and integer-programming certification over arbitrary linearly ordered fields in Mathlib4 (gatermann-parrilo2004, conti-traverso1991, sturmfels-thomas1997):

  • Symmetry-reduced conic duality and strict complementary slackness (SymmetryReducedDualCertificate). Proves weak and exact zero-gap primal--dual optimality over generic ordered fields, group-equivariant Reynolds averaging onto Wedderburn central sectors, and support-uniqueness certification on inactive dual-slack indices without invoking floating-point arithmetic.
  • Explicit algebraic radical shadow prices (ECatRadicalShadowPriceEvaluation). Evaluates closed-form dual multipliers on rank-deficient central cones where one sector lies in the trace radical.
  • Toric binomial Gröbner and Graver bases (NuclearChamberGS, ConfinementLayerTower). Formalises confluent binomial rewriting systems over finitely generated exponent monoids \mathbb{N}^k, strict cost-drop certificates across normal-form promotions, and multi-layer stoichiometric composition towers.
rem:lean-lib-compact-quantum-metrics:
Remark Community Library 4 (CompactQuantumMetrics): Ordered-field Rieffel Lipschitz seminorms and Kantorovich duality. CompactQuantumMetrics formalises Rieffel's theory of compact quantum metric spaces (rieffel1999, rieffel2004) and spectral-triple metric obstructions (connes1994) in purely algebraic ordered-field generality:

  • Lipschitz seminorms and scalar-kernel quotient criteria (FiniteRieffelQuantumMetric, Geometry). Defines order-unit spaces equipped with a seminorm L whose kernel equals the scalar multiples \mathbb{F}\cdot\mathbf{1}, proving boundedness of the induced Monge--Kantorovich metric d_L(\varphi, \psi) = \sup\{|\varphi(a) - \psi(a)| : L(a) \le 1\} on the state space when the quotient A / \mathbb{F}\mathbf{1} has finite radius.
  • Degenerate-trace spectral-triple obstructions (GramDegeneracyBlocksConnes). Proves that any GNS representation built from a trace functional with non-trivial radical \mathrm{rad}\,\tau \neq \{0\} fails faithfulness on the ambient algebra and forces passage to the radical quotient before constructing a spectral triple or quantum metric.

Formalises the Jackson difference operator D_q f(x) = (f(qx) - f(x))/((q-1)x), the discrete Thomae--Jackson definite integral \int_0^a f(x)\,\mathrm{d}_q x = (1-q)a\sum_{k=0}^\infty q^k f(q^k a), the q-fundamental theorem of calculus, q-integration by parts, and monotone Riemann-sum bounds (ThomaeJacksonCoulombAndAlphaTunneling).
  • Symmetric vs Gaussian q-integers and Habiro cyclotomic tails (QIntegerConventions, Habiro). Separates balanced quantum integers [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) from Gaussian polynomials \{n\}_q = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} q^j via the proved bridge q^{n-1}[n]_q = \{n\}_{q^2}, and formalises rising q-Pochhammer products (q;q)_m together with bar-involution parity identities (q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}).

sec:notation-register-section-intro:
Reading convention: every object here is mathematical by default. The symbols in these tables name constructions inside the model. Where a construction is named after a physical entity — electron, proton, neutron, mass, binding energy, decay width — the name is expository, in the same way a topologist names a knot "the trefoil". Writing \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} asserts a quantity defined by the framework, not a claim about the physical proton.

The empirical content of this paper is located precisely at the points where a model quantity is set against a measured one — AME2020, CODATA, PDG. Those comparisons are the physical claims of the work, and they are marked as such where they occur. Everything upstream of a comparison is mathematics, and should be read and checked as mathematics.

Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, an incomplete derivation upstream is a gap in the mathematics, not a defect in the empirical claims that are made. Second, and more demanding: because the physics enters only at the comparison points, those points carry the entire empirical burden. A systematic uncertainty affecting a compared quantity is therefore more consequential under this reading, not less — it acts on the one place where the paper makes contact with measurement.

prose:notation-collisions:
A handful of common letters carry overloaded meanings in the literature. One enforces the following conventions throughout this paper to disambiguate them:

  • c = color (never charm; charm is \mathfrak{c}).

  • b = generic variable (never bottom quark; bottom is \mathfrak{b}).

  • p = brane point (never proton number; proton number is Z).

  • E alone = not used for an exceptional divisor, energy, or elliptic curve. One uses \mathcal{S}_p, \mathfrak{E}, or \mathcal{E}_q respectively. E_{\mathfrak{H}} (with hadron subscript) is allowed for crossing energy.

  • \mathfrak{E} bare = the energy \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 of a braid class (mass--energy equivalence). Every other energy carries a subscript: \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} (crossing energy, which is a different quantity), \mathfrak{E}_0, \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}, \mathfrak{E}_{\gamma}, \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{pole}}. The Euler–Lagrange operator is \mathrm{EL}.

  • \mathfrak{E}_0 vs Q_\beta(n) — two distinct hadronic-sector scalars historically conflated in Python compute scripts. They are not interchangeable:

    • \mathfrak{E}_0 = hadronic energy scale. One derives this as \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)} = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) \approx 4.186 MeV (from m_e and q_0 only). The tower-summed form is \mathfrak{E}_0^{\text{full}} = \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)}/(1-\hbar_q^2) \approx 4.228 MeV. It sets the MeV-per-dimensionless-trace-unit conversion for hadronic predictions.
    • Q_\beta(n) = 0.78233341\,\text{MeV} = the free-neutron \beta-decay Q-value. One relates this to the bar-skew \beta-channel (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}). One uses it as the binding-energy-scale multiplier in Categorical mass as Markov trace's explicit binding formula B = Q_\beta(n) \cdot (|\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}})| - |\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})|). The ratio is \mathfrak{E}_0/Q_\beta(n) = 1/|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \approx 5.31 (the dimensionless Hecke NF reduction). Using \mathfrak{E}_0 for a Q_\beta-valued binding-scale quantity is a registered notation violation.

  • \gamma = three reserved meanings, all standard, disambiguated by context: (i) the photon (default reading in particle / QED contexts: pair production \gamma\gamma \to e^+ e^-, photonic channels, Breit–Wheeler vertices); (ii) the Euler–Mascheroni constant (only inside zeta-value identities, e.g. \zeta'(0) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\log(2\pi), \gamma = \lim(H_n - \log n)); (iii) Dirac matrices \gamma^\mu (always with an explicit Lorentz index). One never uses \gamma for a vortex or closed cycle — the vortex morphism is \varrho.

  • c_k vs \mathrm{cl}_k — the letter c carried three distinct coefficient families, two of them within ~12% of each other numerically, which is how they stayed conflated. One now splits them:

    • c_k = Q_\beta precision-ladder coefficients only, Q_\beta = Q_{\text{base}}\prod_k(1 + c_k u^k) with u = b\hbar_q^2 — dimensionless, c_2 = -1, c_3 = -2 a near-match. (This register fixes the symbol; each rung's epistemic tier and its convention scoping live in the c_k/d_k canonical registry. The word "proved" previously appeared on c_2 here and is removed as a symbol-level claim — the identity re-reads the N{=}2 factor rather than deriving it. "Taylor-exact" was NOT removed for being false, and must not be: c_2 genuinely is the u^2 coefficient of the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k). It is \tilde c_2 = -9/8 only for the normalised series with the cosine factor inside — so always say which series. No tier is changed by this edit.)
    • \tilde c_k = the normalised-series coefficients of the same ladder model: the u^k coefficients of \Phi(u)/\Phi(0) rather than of the explicit factors. The tilde marks a different normalisation of the same object — deliberately not justified by the old w_\lambda / \tilde w_\lambda pairing, which this same register retired in the entry below. The two families are not interchangeable: the model's cosine factor contributes at every order, and \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 exactly, independently of the phase \alpha, so the committed c_2 = -1 has \tilde c_2 = -9/8. Both are correct — one model at two normalisations. The -1/8 is contributed entirely by the half-argument in \cos(\alpha - u/2).
    • c_k^{\mathrm{even}} = the bar-even part of the ladder data, exact in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt 3) — a third object, read as neither c_k nor \tilde c_k.
    • \mathrm{cl}_k = cluster / Ursell coefficients of the many-body expansion — MeV-valued. \mathrm{cl}_3 = -\mathfrak{E}_0\,\Delta^2 g is the three-body cluster coefficient of the \mu_3 door (\mu_3 > 0 \iff \Delta^2 g < 0), and the Borromean H_9 magnitude lift is the same family. One never writes a bare c_k for a cluster coefficient, and never quotes a c_k value without saying which of c_k / \tilde c_k / c_k^{\mathrm{even}} it is — the three differ at the same k (-1, -9/8, \approx -7.4588 at k = 2). Rationale for the roman two-letter tag rather than a new single letter: every single Roman letter is either register-claimed or produces a same-domain case-collision (X_k vs the knot object X_K; Y_k vs the Markov weight y_\lambda; Z = proton number; W_\lambda = geometric weight; j vs the Jones polynomial J_K(q)). This follows the same resolution already used for \mathrm{Sk} (Skein module, moved off \mathcal{S}) and h_{\mathrm{A}} (Hecke amplitude, moved off bare H_A).

  • \chi_q = Lyapunov exponent (distinct from \chi_\zeta(c), the character).

  • Euler characteristic is \chi_{\mathrm{eu}} — never a bare \chi. The glyph \chi is shared by three register-claimed families: the characters \chi_\lambda (Frobenius pairing \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda) and \chi_\zeta(c); the Lyapunov exponent \chi_q above; and the Euler characteristic, which keeps the standard glyph but always carries the roman subscript: \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}. A bare \chi is a notation violation in all three senses. When a total and its strata both appear one subscripts further rather than overload: \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M) for the whole moduli, \chi_{\mathrm{eu},i} for the i-th Behrend stratum. The DT setting is where this bites — a Donaldson–Thomas count is a Behrend-weighted Euler characteristic \sum_i n_i\,\chi_{\mathrm{eu},i}, whose unweighted total \sum_i \chi_{\mathrm{eu},i} = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M) is a different number. (Write \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}, not an uppercase "\Chi": there is no such KaTeX/LaTeX macro — uppercase Greek chi is glyph-identical to Latin X and has no control sequence, so it fails the render gate. The orbifold Euler number of \Sigma(2,3,5) keeps its own conventional symbol e = -1/30.)

  • -2 vs -6 in the Stokes/DT sector — two integers that are not the same object and must not be swapped. \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} \Delta_\lambda = -2 is the QOU Wedderburn/Springer Euler characteristic and is the prefactor of the GGM sandwich A \cdot W_{-1} \cdot B \cdot W_{-1}^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot C = -2\,S^{+}(0). The sandwich (0,1) entry is -6 = (-2)\cdot 3 — the prefactor times the Stokes/DT count S^{+}(0)_{01} = 3 — and is not an Euler characteristic, notwithstanding the G3 directive's "Euler = -6" hint. Cite -2 for the Euler characteristic and 3 for the count.

  • \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) names three different objects, and two corpus claims about it are in direct conflict — resolve the symbol to its object before quoting a value. Euler-characteristic stability fixes one bridge, \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A_n) := \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n), the topological Euler characteristic of the total space. Three live sites then read it three ways. (i) Bring's Euler characteristic takes the generic fibre of \mathcal{S} to be Bring's surface \Sigma_4 and so reports -6. (ii) Quantum characteristic classes for SU(2) takes \mathcal{S} = \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong \mathbb{CP}^1 and so reports \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2. These are the same bridge applied to different \mathcal{S}, and the two disagree about the fibre — genus 4 against genus 0 — so at most one of them describes the state bundle of the Descartes universe. (iii) Knot-operator selection writes \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \approx 2.0108968667 at the proton q_0. That is \dim_q of the fundamental V_1, not of the base algebra A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) — a third object, sharing only the glyph. The conflict is one of objects, not of notation. Substrate line bundle: base not fibre states that \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is strictly independent of q, while Bring's Euler characteristic's own proof recovers the -6 as "the quantum dimension specialised at the Descartes substrate parameter q_0". A quantity independent of q does not need specialising at q_0, and reading (iii) is manifestly q-dependent. Resolution — reading (iii) is the categorical trace: \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = \dim_q(A), the quantum dimension, i.e. the Euler characteristic of an object in the QOU category. Three consequences follow. (1) \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is q-DEPENDENT. So substrate line bundle: base not fibre's bullet — "\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) is strictly independent of q" — is withdrawn. Its four sibling bullets (\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)), c_1, c_2, the Euler class e(\xi)) are untouched; only the trace bullet moves. (2) The integers -6 and 2 are TOPOLOGICAL Euler characteristics \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}), a different object from the categorical trace. They are therefore not competing values of one quantity, and neither is "wrong" — but Euler-characteristic stability's bridge \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n) is now a substantive claim relating two different things, not a restatement: it equates a q-dependent quantity with a q-independent integer, so it can hold at most on a locus in q unless a regularisation is supplied. Whether that locus contains q_0 is open. (3) Bring's Euler characteristic's proof is now in the right register, and the ruling FORCES a regularisation on it. Its "the quantum dimension of A specialises at q_0 to -6" is the correct kind of statement under the ruling. Measured in exact arithmetic at 50 digits (8/8 checks): \dim_q(V_n) = [n+1]_q is positive and strictly increasing, with infimum [1]_q = 1, so -6 is not the naive quantum dimension of any finite-dimensional irrep. But the sharper fact is about A itself. A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is not an irrep — by Peter–Weyl it is \bigoplus_n V_n \otimes V_n^{*}, so its naive quantum dimension is \sum_n [n+1]_q^2, whose terms grow like q^{2n}. At q_0 > 1 that diverges: consecutive-term ratio 1.23205245417 at n = 120, partial sum already 1.12 \times 10^{13}. So the naive \dim_q(A) is not a real number at q_0 at all — a regularisation is not an optional refinement of the -6 reading, it is required before \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) has a value, and the ruling is what forces that. Alternating sums over the same tower do reach negatives (\sum_{k=0}^{3} (-1)^k [k+1]_q = -2.0769), which is the shape a -6 would have to come from; that the corpus's -6 arises that way is not claimed. Scope (b) for the divergence, invariant = a series with consecutive-term ratio above 1; scope (a) for the rest. Archimedean / fibre / forgetful functors. Three nominally similar functors appear in the QOU framework and must not be conflated:

Functor Domain → Codomain Role
Fibre functor \tau \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch} Tannakian fibre over a brane point; selects which substrate object becomes the observation.
Forgetful functor U \mathbf{Arch} \to \mathbf{Vec}_{\mathbb{R}} Drops the archimedean enrichment, leaving the underlying real vector space.
Archimedean realisation (informal "Arch") \mathbf{C}(R) \to \mathbf{C}(\mathbb{R}) Base-ring substitution (R ↦ ℝ) at the archimedean wall; not a functor between QOU categories.

The category \mathbf{Arch} is the target of \tau, not the name of a functor. When authoring, one says which one: "\tau specialised to \mathbf{Arch}" or "the R \mapsto \mathbb{R} realisation". One never writes "the archimedean realisation" without context.

Pinning \tau's codomain — one functor, several de-enriched levels. The canonical fibre functor is \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch}. Where \tau is written into a different target, it means a composite with \tau, not a rival functor:

Written as Means Level
\tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch} the fibre functor itself enriched (canonical)
\tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Vec}_{\mathbb{R}} U \circ \tau forget archimedean enrichment
\tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Type} underlying set-valued functor (Tannakian \omega) forget linear structure
\tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{D} (spatial realisation) \tau into a chosen geometric model \mathbf{D} model-specific

These are genuine functors (they act on morphisms). What is not a functor is the archimedean evaluation \pi_\infty \colon \mathrm{Obj}(\mathbf{Arch}) \to \mathbb{R} (an object-level map / place), and the ring-level realisations it induces: the motivic measure \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} \colon K_0(\mathrm{Var}) \to \mathbb{R} (a ring homomorphism) and the standard-part map \mathrm{st} \colon \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R} (a ring homomorphism). Reserve "functor" for \tau, U, and \mathrm{St}; call the maps into \mathbb{R} realisations / evaluations.

"Forgetful functor \tau" (classical usage) — a synonym, not a clash. The core definition blocks write "the forgetful functor \tau" (e.g. a QOU is a (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) with the forgetful functor \tau faithful; Quantum Observable Universe), and Notation: the forgetful functor \tau names \tau "the forgetful functor". This is the classical Tannakian name: for \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}(U_q\mathfrak{sl}_2) the fibre functor and the forgetful functor are the same functor \tau — the one \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Mod}_R that forgets the coaction, keeping the underlying module. In the enriched register above that classical \tau is the composite U \circ \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Vec}_{\mathbb{R}} (row 2 of the previous table); the faithfulness axiom is a statement about this underlying-module level. So "forgetful functor \tau" and "fibre functor \tau" name the same genuine functor at different codomain levels — the only distinct forgetful arrow is the intermediate U \colon \mathbf{Arch} \to \mathbf{Vec}_{\mathbb{R}}. This is naming synonymy, not a functor-vs-map error: \tau is a genuine functor under either name, so the core-block wording needs no change.

rem:glossary-hom-set:
Remark Hom-set. Hom-set. For objects X and Y in a category \mathbf{C}, the hom-set \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(X, Y) is the collection of all morphisms from X to Y. It is also written \mathbf{C}(X, Y) or X \to Y. In a locally small category, each hom-set is a genuine set.

When \mathbf{C} is R-linear, each hom-set carries the structure of an R-module. Composition is R-bilinear.
rem:glossary-monoidal-category: Remark Monoidal category. Monoidal category. A category \mathbf{C} equipped with a bifunctor \otimes \colon \mathbf{C} \times \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{C}, a distinguished unit object \mathbf{1}, and coherent natural isomorphisms for associativity (\alpha), left unitality (\lambda), and right unitality (\rho). These satisfy Mac Lane's pentagon and triangle axioms.
rem:glossary-braided-monoidal-category: Remark Braided monoidal category. Braided monoidal category. A monoidal category equipped with a natural isomorphism \beta_{X,Y} \colon X \otimes Y \xrightarrow{\sim} Y \otimes X satisfying the two hexagon axioms.
rem:glossary-symmetric-monoidal-category: Remark Symmetric monoidal category. Symmetric monoidal category. A braided monoidal category whose braiding is involutive: \beta_{Y,X} \circ \beta_{X,Y} = \mathrm{id}_{X \otimes Y}.
rem:glossary-monoidal-functor:
Remark Monoidal functor. Monoidal functor. A functor F \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{D} between monoidal categories equipped with a natural transformation \mu_{X,Y} \colon F(X) \otimes F(Y) \to F(X \otimes Y) and a morphism \epsilon \colon \mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{D}} \to F(\mathbf{1}_{\mathbf{C}}). These are compatible with the associator and unitors.

The functor is lax monoidal when \mu and \epsilon are arbitrary morphisms and strong monoidal when they are isomorphisms.
